title: [Ruling] The `/meta` type segment is ALWAYS singular — retire every plural spelling, no exception, in three steps
body:
**Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-16.** Provenance: live PM chat, session `session_01NTKPDRoynY8i3HmdSFUxFj`, `domain:metadata` seat (#6367). Verbatim:

> 「这是创业项目,目前用户很少,三个自有仓库里没人硬编码, 一刀切「删除所有复数」是不是从长远看损失更小」
> 「把这个裁决(一刀切 + 三步)立成卡、并起 ① 的实施卡」

## The ruling

**The `/meta` type segment is singular. Always. There is no exception and no tolerated plural alias.**

⛔ Not re-litigable. What remains open is sequencing and per-site shape, not the direction.

## What this is NOT

- ⛔ **Not** a change to `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR`'s legitimate job. The manifest-collection map still names stack collections; what is retired is its use as a **fold below a folding boundary**.
- ⛔ **Not** a claim that any stored plural row becomes reachable. Pre-#7894 at-rest residue stays unreachable and now fails loudly (#9111 / PR #9173). This ruling does not launder it.
- ⛔ **Not** a licence to blank a diagnostic or soften a refusal. Every refusal added under this ruling **must name the canonical spelling** — the `metaUrlSpellingRefusal` shape, not a bare 400. A guided migration, not a wall.

## The three steps — ruled order, and the order is load-bearing

| # | step | card | why this position |
|---|---|---|---|
| **①** | **Read verbs refuse plurals, like the write verbs already do** — `historyMetaItem`, `auditMetaItem`, `findReferencesToMeta` | **#9157** | ⭐ **The only step with a demonstrated harm.** Today a plural read answers `{ events: [] }` / `{ references: [] }` — *"nothing depends on this"* delivered at exactly the moment someone is about to rename or delete. Safety first, and it is independently valuable even if ② and ③ never ship. |
| **②** | **State route**: point `meta.getLegalNextStates` at the singular twin, delete the plural registration, delete the registration-order pin the collision required | *to file* | Depends on nothing; deferrable; the only step with any external-break exposure |
| **③** | **Docs + the fold's retirement**: `metadata-api.mdx:26` becomes "types are singular"; `PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR` stops being consulted as a fold (see also **#9174**) | *to file* | Last, because it should describe a world that already exists |

Each step is independently revertible. ⛔ Do not bundle them.

## The measurement that carried it

Swept `objectstack`, `objectui` and `cloud` at the maintainer's direction. Every probe ran with a positive control, because a zero from a mis-shaped probe is the error this seat made twice today.

| repo | literal plural **item** routes | variable-typed item routes | control |
|---|---|---|---|
| objectui | **0** | 1 — `DraftChangesPanel.tsx:112` | 29 files with singular item routes ✅ |
| cloud | **0** | 1 — `scripts/eval/golden-prompts.mjs:184` | 2 ✅ |
| objectstack | 0 generic; the `/meta/objects/:name/state/:field` hits are a **declared** route, not a tolerance | 4 — the client SDK | 41 ✅ |

**Nobody hardcodes a plural item route in any of the three repos.** Two facts qualify that:

- The SDK's `type` is `string` — `getItem` / `saveItem` / `deleteItem` / `getHistory` impose **no type-level guard**.
- `DraftChangesPanel` takes `type` **straight from the `/meta/_drafts` feed's stored rows** (`d.type as string`, `typeof` check only, no fold) and interpolates it into an item route ⇒ a stored plural makes the Console emit a plural request. Data-driven, not authored.

## ⛔ Two things I got wrong, corrected by measurement

**1. I priced the state route as a hard constraint.** I argued that deleting the plural "breaks a published SDK method". The ledger says both spellings are mounted — `:195` plural `disposition: sdk`, `:197` singular `disposition: server-only`. **The singular twin already exists.** The migration is one string in our own SDK, and it *deletes* a collision plus the registration-order pin that exists only to manage it. I let "this is published surface" act as a **stop sign** instead of a **cost to be priced**. #8739's *"the docs are the promise already made"* forbids breaking a promise **silently** — it does not forbid changing a published surface deliberately.

**2. I claimed `/meta/apps` was a live plural caller in objectui.** It is not. All six hits are **comments**; there is no fetch, and **no such route exists in the ledger**. Filed separately as a docs-drift finding.

## The argument that decided it, which was the maintainer's

**One rule can be put in a type and pinned by a gate. One rule plus one exception cannot** — it requires every future author, and every AI author, to know which family they are in. ⭐ **That is precisely the defect class that has already cost roughly ten cards** (#4432 · #7894 · #8769 · #8819 · #8820 · #8862 · #8908 · #9009 · #9111 · #9157 · #9174).

I wrote in my own analysis that "an exception is exactly what an AI author gets wrong" and then recommended keeping one. The inconsistency was mine.

The cost asymmetry is the whole case: **a breaking change's window closes monotonically; an exception's cost accumulates monotonically. Today is the cheapest this will ever be.** Startup, very few users, zero internal hardcoding.

## ⚠️ The one thing still unmeasured, and why it did not block

Whether an **external** caller hand-rolls HTTP against `/meta/objects/:name/state/:field`. Three self-owned repos cannot answer that — only cloud's access logs can. `git grep` answers *"nobody here hardcodes it"*, which is **not** *"nobody uses it"*; those two look identical in a probe's output.

Ruled to proceed anyway: the exposure is confined to step **②**, affects only whether that step needs a deprecation window, and **does not touch the direction**. Step ① carries no external exposure at all.
